title: Mixtape and Detention
premise: Hazel Pemberton has survived high school by being nobody: a coder who runs an anonymous account, @detentionfiles, that documents the town of Marrow Creek's century-old 'Mixtape' tradition—a senior-year ritual that quietly decides who belongs and who gets erased. When her best friend Priya vanishes on the night she was supposed to be crowned Mixtape royalty, leaving only her car keys in the school's boiler room, Hazel's anonymous posts become both evidence and target. Following Priya's trail through the town's founding families, a burned-down rec center, and the school's sealed 1974 time capsule, Hazel discovers the Mixtape isn't a party—it's a cover for the founding families' control over land deeds, scholarships, and silence. With three days until the ceremony, Hazel must choose between exposing everything (and burning the found family she's built with outcast seniors Dev and Marisol) or playing along to find Priya alive. In the end, Hazel broadcasts the truth mid-ceremony, Priya is found locked in the old rec center basement—alive, having uncovered the same secret—and the town's tradition collapses, replaced by something messier but honest.
about_author: Kestrel Oyelaran is a former small-town radio DJ turned software engineer who writes stories about kids who fix what adults broke. They live in Ohio with a rescue greyhound and a wall of unlabeled cassette tapes.

chapters.title: Head Down, Grades Up
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. We meet Hazel mid-anonymity: coding in the library, running @detentionfiles from behind seven proxies, watching Priya shine as the school's golden girl and Mixtape frontrunner. A post about the tradition's shady scholarship committee gets flagged by the principal. Emotional beat: the comfort and loneliness of invisibility.

chapters.title: The Night of the Keys
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Priya texts Hazel a single voice memo—half a sentence about 'the basement'—then goes silent. Hazel finds her car abandoned outside school, keys left neatly in the boiler room lock. The police call it a runaway. Emotional beat: dread crystallizing into resolve; Hazel breaks her own rules and posts publicly for the first time.

chapters.title: Dev, Marisol, and the Detention Table
chapters.summary: Alternating POV with Dev Okonkwo, a repeat-senior mechanic's kid who knows every crawl space in the building. He and Marisol Reyes—the only student ever formally 'uninvited' from the Mixtape—join Hazel's search. Emotional beat: three outsiders becoming a unit; found family begins to form around shared suspicion.

chapters.title: What the Account Knew
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Someone replies to @detentionfiles with photos of Priya taken hours before she vanished—and a warning: stop digging or the account's real identity gets posted. Hazel realizes whoever runs the Mixtape has been reading her all along. Emotional beat: paranoia; the hunter realizing she's also prey.

chapters.title: The Ashfield Deed
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Digging through county records, Hazel finds the 1974 time capsule listed alongside a land deed: the Mixtape crowns a 'heir' who inherits quiet control of the town's property trust. Every winner for fifty years has been a founding-family kid—except one year: 1998, when a winner's name was scratched out. Emotional beat: revelation; the tradition reframed as machinery.

chapters.title: Nineteen Ninety-Eight
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. Dev tracks down the scratched-out winner: his aunt Ruthie, who left town at seventeen and never said why. Her testimony reveals the ceremony's back rooms, the 'obligations' winners sign, and what happens to kids who refuse. Emotional beat: grief and fury; the past reaching into the present.

chapters.title: Three Days
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. The committee offers Hazel a deal: delete the account, play nice, and Priya comes home. They attach proof-of-life—a photo timestamped that morning. Hazel has seventy-two hours before the ceremony. Emotional beat: moral vertigo; loyalty to Priya weaponized against the truth.

chapters.title: The Boiler Room Tape
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Decoding the half-voice-memo against the school's PA hum, the trio pinpoints where it was recorded: the sealed sub-basement under the old rec center, accessible only through the boiler room. They map a way in—but the committee changes the locks. Emotional beat: terror sharpening into plan; the team commits fully.

chapters.title: Ceremony
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. During the Mixtape ceremony, while the town watches, Hazel and Dev slip below; Marisol hijacks the AV booth. Hazel finds Priya chained in the flooded sub-basement archive—surrounded by fifty years of signed obligations—and Marisol puts the whole archive on the gymnasium projector. Emotional beat: climax; truth detonated in front of everyone.

chapters.title: Side B
chapters.summary: Priya's POV, then Hazel's. Priya recounts her own investigation and captivity; the founding families fracture under exposure, the trust dissolves into community hands. The four friends hold their own anti-Mixtape in the parking lot—burner phones, bad speakers, everyone invited. Emotional beat: bittersweet resolution; visibility chosen, family kept, justice imperfect but real.
